messages.subject: histogram (Freq) with distribution curve
parts:
Dear list,

I am trying to produce a histogram (Freq) overlaid by a distribution
curve with ggplot2. (Which seems not to be sooo clever
http://finzi.psych.upenn.edu/R/Rhelp02/archive/37166.html)
This is my code so far:

source("http://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/data.r")
library(ggplot2)
df.mean <- round( mean(df$energie), 2)
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = energie) )
p <- p + geom_histogram(colour = "black",
fill = alpha("grey", 0.70), binwidth = 0.25)
p <- p + scale_x_continuous(paste("Energie", df$light, df.mean,
df$co, sep = " - "), limits=c(0, 12) ) + scale_y_continuous
("Count")
p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = df$xlow, size=0.75,
colour = alpha("blue", 0.70))
p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = df$m, size=0.75,
colour = alpha("red", 0.70))
p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = df$xhigh, size=0.75,
colour = alpha("blue", 0.70))
p <- p + theme_bw()
print(p)

So, how can I overlay this plot with the distribution curve?

2.
The graphic should look like this http://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/dokument2.pdf
I don't know how to split or rearrange the plot for the textfield on
the right. I think I have to play with "grid"?...

Thanks for any help!!
Patrick

It appears that http://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/data.r automatically
redirects to https://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/data.r, and if you try
this url directly, you'll see the real problem:

source("https://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/data.r")

Hadley

messages.author: b26ea422f70d3a1f
messages.subject: Re: histogram (Freq) with distribution curve

Hadley,

You beat me by a minute or so...

To add a tip, at least on MacOS X (and other UNIX's with curl), you
can make this particular instance work with:

source (pipe ("curl -s 'https://www.davidwilke.de/hausmann/
data.r'"))

which uses the curl command to handle the https connection. (Your curl
has to be configured to support SSL, which I assume most installations
do.)

Wayne
